title: 2-Year Treasury Yield (DGS2)
summary: The 2-Year Treasury Yield increased 12 basis points over the week ending April 23, 2026, rising from 3.71% to 3.83%. The most recent daily change was +4 bps on April 23. This is raw market data from FRED with no analyst commentary or causal attribution provided.
key_points: Week-over-week change: +12 bps (from 3.71% on 2026-04-17 to 3.83% on 2026-04-23)
Data source: FRED series DGS2 (constant maturity)
No narrative or explanation provided for the yield movement
why_it_matters: The 2-year yield is highly sensitive to near-term Fed rate expectations and serves as a market-based proxy for policy rate expectations over the next 2 years. A 12-bp weekly rise suggests either firming rate-cut expectations being unwound or increasing growth/inflation concerns pricing into the front end of the curve.
macro_context: Rising 2-year yields typically reflect tightening financial conditions and can signal reduced expectations for Fed rate cuts or heightened growth/inflation concerns. The directional bias toward risk-off reflects that higher short-term rates increase borrowing costs and can compress equity valuations.
